card.name: Add-on therapy and comparison arms
card.fires_on: Words in clinical trial text describing a drug given in addition to, or compared with, another treatment, such as 'therapy' after 'best available', 'to' after 'added' or 'in addition', and plural endings of disease or drug terms.

modes.label: Add-on or comparator wording
modes.description: Linking words and endings where a drug is added to or compared with standard treatment.
modes.example: in addition<< to>> standard of care

modes.label: Ends of group or disease names
modes.description: Final piece of a plural drug or disease term inside a patient-group description.
modes.example: in patients with histiocytic neoplas<<ms>>, 19% of patients experienced

modes.label: Ranges and class lists
modes.description: Words linking numbers or classes in a list, such as 'to' in a dose range or 'and' between classes.

card.writes: It seems to promote words like 'mostly' and 'at least', which suggests quantity or proportion wording comes next.
card.plain: It fires on small words in trial text where one treatment is added to or compared with another.
